So path + commonGitDir + worktreeGitDir all match across a destroy-and-recreate, and cleanupSeatLinkedWorktrees' identity test passes for a tree the record was never written for. THE DISCRIMINATOR WAS IN THE SAME EXPERIMENT: the admin directory inode CHANGED (657687295 -> 657687443) while every string stayed the same. So the smallest generation binding is dev+ino of worktreeGitDir, recorded at registration and re-verified at reclaim. Two stronger forms if inode reuse worries you: record the worktree's HEAD sha and branch at registration and require both still to match; or - exact, and free because the seat's wrapper already OBSERVES the creation - mint a random uuid marker file inside the admin directory at creation, record it in the row, require it at reclaim. A recreated tree carries no marker and a re-registered tree carries a different one, so a stale row can never match.
